controls.title: Event logging — organization-defined event types are selected for logging
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That the selection of event types was appropriate to the system or organization-defined needs. The chain receives what is configured to be sent.
controls.what_we_prove: Events submitted to the chain are stored with tamper-evident ordering, signed timestamps, and cryptographic anchoring. The event-logging implementation is verifiable end-to-end.

controls.title: Content of audit records — required information fields are present
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That the submitted records contained all the required content fields per organization policy. The chain is content-agnostic; field-completeness is the emitter's responsibility.
controls.what_we_prove: The chain preserves the exact content of each audit record as submitted, with no possibility of after-the-fact field modification. An auditor can verify the record content has not been altered.

controls.title: Audit record review, analysis, and reporting
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That the review was substantive, that anomalies were correctly identified, or that reports were actioned. The chain attests the activity; the rigor is the organization's call.
controls.what_we_prove: Review and analysis events (who reviewed which records, when, what was reported) submitted to the chain are stored with tamper-evident ordering. The review actually happened as recorded.

controls.title: Protection of audit information — audit records and audit logging tools are protected from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That audit records were protected during the path from emitter to chain. The chain enforces immutability from the point of inclusion forward.
controls.what_we_prove: Once submitted to the chain, audit records cannot be modified or deleted without producing a mathematically detectable break in the hash-linked chain. Modification or deletion is fail-loud, not silent.

controls.title: Non-repudiation — actions cannot be plausibly denied
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That the human or system principal whose key signed the event was the actual originator of the underlying action. The chain non-repudiates the cryptographic emission; the upstream identity binding (and the integrity of the signing key itself) is the organization's responsibility.
controls.what_we_prove: Events in the chain are signed under customer-bound keys. An auditor can mathematically attribute each event to the signing identity; absent a claim of key compromise, the identity cannot plausibly deny the event's authenticity.

controls.title: Audit record generation — capability to generate audit records exists
controls.what_we_dont_prove: That every required event type was wired to emit records. The chain receives submissions; the generation configuration is the system owner's responsibility.
controls.what_we_prove: The chain attests that audit records were generated and recorded, with provable timestamps and ordering. Generation capability is exercised end-to-end.

controls_out_of_scope.reason: access control family is policy-level (specific access events may be logged but the access control system is not chain-evidenced)
assessment, authorization, and monitoring is process-level (overlaps with AU-6 above)
incident response is procedural (specific incident events may be logged)
physical and environmental protection is physical
system and services acquisition is contractual
system and communications protection is system-level
system and information integrity is system-level (SI-7 software integrity may overlap with AU-9 but is system-level)
supply chain risk management is contractual
PII processing and transparency is policy-level
